title: smime-tree: String-carrying error variants lose structured information
description:
Why this exists: smime_tree/src/error.rs has six variants in SmimeError that wrap String: Other(String), MalformedInput(String), RngFailure(String), DecryptionFailed(String), UnsupportedAlgorithm(String), WrongContentType(String). CertChainError also has Other(String). The Rust coding standard states: 'Error variants must carry structured fields, not String messages — Err(format\!("expected {x}, got {y}")) loses the values.'

What goes wrong: a String-carrying variant loses the underlying values. A caller that wants to match on UnsupportedAlgorithm to log the OID separately, or retry with a fallback algorithm, has to parse a String — which is fragile and not semver-safe. Code that matches on SmimeError::UnsupportedAlgorithm(s) and inspects s is doing ad-hoc string parsing. Structured variants allow pattern matching on individual fields without fragility.

Locations: smime-tree/src/error.rs — SmimeError::Other, MalformedInput, RngFailure, DecryptionFailed, UnsupportedAlgorithm, WrongContentType; CertChainError::Other.

Fix: replace each String with one or more typed fields. For example, UnsupportedAlgorithm { oid: der::asn1::ObjectIdentifier } and WrongContentType { expected: String, actual: String } (where type names are stable identifiers, not free-form messages).
close_reason: P2 refactoring: String-carrying error variants (Other, MalformedInput, etc.) are catch-alls for diverse failure modes. A comprehensive structured error overhaul is a separate effort.
